findings.finding: Legacy normalisation assigns `legacy-<n>` ids. If a profile mixes objects and strings, a user-authored rule could legitimately have id `legacy-1`, colliding with a normalised string — "first wins, later is an error" would then reject a valid user rule. The plan doesn't say whether legacy ids are collision-checked against declared ids.

findings.finding: check_paths` uses realpath + containment, which resolves symlinks at check time but the path can be repointed afterwards (TOCTOU). For a config-validation use case this is mostly fine — the check is diagnostic, not a security gate — but the docstring shouldn't imply containment is guaranteed.
findings.suggestion: Document the check as point-in-time validation only. No code change needed.

findings.finding: Bundled profiles skip `check_paths` at runtime (different installed-cache layout), relying solely on a repo test. If a future bundled profile adds a mechanism with a wrong path and the repo test is skipped or not wired into the default test target, the gap goes unnoticed.

Legacy rules are appended to `RuleSet.rules` after all object rules, so a mixed list `["Old.", rule_a, rule_b]` yields ordering `[a, b, legacy-string-1]` rather than profile order. A future renderer that assumes rules follow profile order will render legacy sentences last. This is documented behaviour ("a declared id always beats a generated one") but the reordering side effect is not.
findings.suggestion: Either sort the output back into profile position order, or note the reordering in the frozen-contract docstring so the U2+ renderer units don't assume positional fidelity.

findings.finding: On a corrupt/unreadable bundled file the function `return None`s immediately instead of `continue`-ing to the next bundled shadow path. With the current lookup model (one bundled profile per name) this is unreachable, but the `shadows` list is a list precisely because callers may pass several.

The corrupt-file test only asserts "no crash / None"; it would also pass if the warning were silently never emitted for a valid bundled file in the same directory. The happy-path shadow warning (bundled has rules → warning emitted) is only covered indirectly through the CLI test in the other file; a direct unit test of `shadow_rules_warning` returning the warning string is missing.
findings.suggestion: Add one assertion where a readable bundled JSON with non-empty `architecture_rules` produces the warning string.

findings.finding: A rule with a valid but duplicate id short-circuits at the `elif rid in seen` branch, so a duplicate that also has shape problems reports only "duplicate id", and conversely a shape-error rule never registers its id in `seen`, so two invalid rules sharing an id each get shape errors rather than a duplicate error. Harmless for consumers (both are dropped), but the diagnostic can mislead.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is; if tightened, report both problems per rule.
